children: Tobin Marcus, head of U.S. policy and politics at Wolfe Research, dismissed President Donald Trump's proposed $5K dividend checks to Americans as both legally unviable and economically ill-timed.
Trump on Wednesday proposed a $5K “Trump dividend” for every adult U.S. citizen if Republicans retain control of
of Congress in November’s midterm elections.

But the president lacks the authority to issue such payments without congressional approval, Marcus told CNBC in an interview Thursday, noting the proposal is "not really macroeconomically appropriate in an environment where inflation's already running uncomfortably warm."

The policy analyst emphasized that no legal authority exists for the president to unilaterally distribute dividend checks. This explains why previous proposals—including so-called "DOGE dividends" and "tariff dividends"—have never materialized into actual payments. Marcus said investors are largely dismissing the latest proposal, noting he has received few questions about its potential macroeconomic impacts.
"I don't think that the American people are gonna take this all that seriously," he said.

The dividend proposal joins other populist campaign promises, including plans to lower credit card swipe fees and cap interest rates. Marcus framed these announcements as attempts to fill an agenda gap ahead of the midterm elections, offering voters a vision of what Republicans would pursue if they retained unified control of government. However, he noted that Republicans holding the House "is not our base case or really anyone else's."

title: Trump's dividend proposal unlikely and macro unsound - Wolfe’s Tobin Marcus
